foods.name: Water and sparkling water
foods.why: The GOAT of pregnancy drinks. Staying hydrated helps with just about everything, and the bubbly kind counts exactly the same as the still kind.

foods.name: Home-made smoothies
foods.why: Your blender, your rules. Pasteurised milk or yoghurt plus washed fruit, blitzed and drunk straight away, is a green light every single time.

foods.name: Pasteurised bottled juice
foods.why: Pasteurised is the magic word. The bottled and carton stuff has already been heat-treated on your behalf, so pour a big one.

foods.name: Decaf coffee
foods.why: Basically a free hug. Near enough to no caffeine, so it sits outside the daily budget and the 4pm one is entirely yours.

foods.name: Coffee
foods.why: Caffeine has a daily cap of 200mg from everything combined. That is roughly 1 to 2 espresso-based coffees, or about 3 cups of instant.
foods.makeItGreen: Keep the whole day under 200mg and your coffee is a green light. The trick is counting the teas and colas in the same tally.
foods.swap: A decaf flat white, or warm milk with cinnamon when the budget is spent.

foods.name: Tea
foods.why: Tea draws on the same 200mg daily caffeine budget as coffee. Around 4 to 5 cups fits inside it, as long as coffee is not also on the tally.
foods.makeItGreen: Keep the day's caffeine total under 200mg and your cuppa is all clear.
foods.swap: A decaf brew, or hot water with lemon when the tally is nearly full.

foods.name: Hot chocolate
foods.why: A hot choc counts toward the 200mg caffeine budget, but it is one of the lightest hitters going. Roughly 4 to 5 cups fits in a day.
foods.makeItGreen: Inside the day's 200mg caffeine total, it is a green light. Made on pasteurised milk at home, it is one of the easy ones.
foods.swap: Warm milk with cinnamon or vanilla: no caffeine, same cosy.

foods.name: Cola
foods.why: Cola carries caffeine, so it lands in the same 200mg daily cap: about 4 to 5 cans fits, shared with your coffees and teas.
foods.makeItGreen: Inside the day's 200mg caffeine total, cola is fine. Caffeine-free versions do not touch the tally at all.
foods.swap: Sparkling water with a big wedge of lime, or a lemonade if it is the fizz you are chasing.

foods.name: Soft drinks and sugary drinks
foods.why: Nothing unsafe here, it is just sometimes-food territory: lots of sugar and not much else. Save them for when you genuinely fancy one.
foods.makeItGreen: Treated as a sometimes drink rather than the daily one, there is nothing to worry about.
foods.swap: Sparkling water with fruit in it, or pasteurised juice topped up with soda water.

foods.name: Artificial sweeteners
foods.why: Fine in moderation, and that really is the whole story. The sweeteners approved for Australian food and drink are safe, there is just no need to go overboard.
foods.makeItGreen: In normal everyday amounts they are a green light.

foods.name: Herbal tea
foods.why: A couple of cups a day of the common flavours, like ginger or peppermint, is the usual advice. Medicinal and slimming blends are a different beast entirely.
foods.makeItGreen: Stick to everyday flavours like ginger, peppermint and chamomile, keep it to a couple of cups, and run any medicinal blend past your midwife first.
foods.swap: Hot water with fresh lemon and a slice of ginger, or a decaf brew.

foods.name: Alcohol
foods.why: No known safe amount in pregnancy, so it sits out the next few months. A splash cooked into a long-simmered sauce is one for your care team to call.
foods.swap: Sparkling water, lime and frozen berries in the good glass, or soda with a splash of pasteurised juice and a fat wedge of orange.

foods.name: Energy drinks
foods.why: Energy drinks stack caffeine with guarana and other stimulants, which blows past the 200mg daily cap quickly. Off the menu for now.
foods.swap: A cold brew that fits inside your caffeine budget, or an icy sparkling water when it is the cold hit you are after.

foods.name: Kombucha, kefir and ginger beer
foods.why: Fermented drinks are brewed with live cultures, so they carry a contamination risk plus a little leftover alcohol. NSW Food Authority says park them for now.
foods.swap: Dry ginger ale over ice for the same spicy fizz, or a fresh ginger tea if it is the tummy-settling you are after.

foods.name: 0.0% beers and zero-alcohol drinks
foods.why: In Australia a drink labelled 0.0 can still legally hold up to 0.5% alcohol. Plenty of people are comfortable with that, and it is a great one to raise at your next appointment.
foods.makeItGreen: Brands that state 0.0% and confirm no detectable alcohol are the safest pick here, and your midwife's take is the one that counts.
foods.swap: Soda water with lime and frozen berries in a proper glass, or a pasteurised juice spritz.

foods.name: Raw milk as a drink
foods.why: Without pasteurisation, listeria and friends stay right where they are in the bottle. This is the one dairy rule with no wiggle room in it.
foods.makeItGreen: Pasteurised milk, including UHT and long life, is a green light and tastes the same in your coffee.
foods.swap: Any pasteurised milk from the fridge aisle, dairy or otherwise.
